newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain in selective trade, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain in selective trade, off highs.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose an average 0.68 percent in range-bound and selective trade on Friday in reaction to Thursday's 2.02 percent drop, but volume was low, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed up 560.73 points at 82,566.84, after moving between 81,888 and 83,303. It gained 0.18 percent over the three-day week after 0.83 percent last week. The market was closed for holiday on Monday and Tuesday.
Trade volume dived to 16.93 trillion lira, including a 2.02 trillion lira block deal on the wholesale market, from Thursday's 19.02 trillion.
"Activity was sales oriented in the afternoon session in contrast to buying in early morning. The market is trying to find a balance at these levels," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank securities.
Brokers were expecting range-bound trade with major support seen at 81,000 after the market failed to pierce the strong 85,000 barrier early on Thursday.

"The index remained squeezed between 81,000-84,000 today. The rapid rise seen in the past two months has slowed down which shows the market is losing strength. I think the market has reached saturation," said Seyfullah Esen from Oki securities.
"There are no driving expectations left. But a downtrend is not awaited unless the index falls below 81,000. It does, it may target 75,000," he said.
The index had surged 29.3 percent from September 13 to an all-time high close of 83,772.33 on October 23, the tenth record in an uptrend which began with the breaching of 65,000 level.
Of the 228 shares traded, 108 gained, 66 lost and 54 closed stable. The 85-share industrial index firmed 0.24 percent to 86,625.08 and the 15-share financial index rose 1.65 percent to 81,147.38.
Top actives were utilities Aktas Elektrik, up 8,000 lira at 95,000 and Cukurova Elektrik, up 1,000 lira at 78,000.
